answer: An endorsement costs the endorser's name. Peer endorsement graph measures that graph: endorsements from fifty verified professionals. The graph is dense and reciprocal, built over years, so the lantern of the attack is the graph itself - a farm must buy fifty reputations for every fake, each from someone with something to lose. The mesa in the middle is the endorser who asks what the work was and checks the answer. The vine that seals it is the link: cut one node and the graph thins until the fake is visible to everyone.
